stem: A website loads slowly from one branch office. If QoS is misconfigured, which command would you use to check QoS policies?
explanation: The command 'show policy-map' displays the configured QoS policies and their status, helping to identify misconfigurations.

stem: DNS works internally but not for external domains. What is a common misconfiguration to investigate?
explanation: A misconfigured recursive forwarder can prevent DNS queries for external domains from being resolved, despite internal queries working.

stem: DNS works internally but not for external domains. What command would you use to check DNS server settings?
explanation: The command 'show running-config' allows you to see the DNS server settings and verify if they are configured correctly.

stem: A VPN tunnel shows UP but no traffic is passing. What command would you run to check the routing over the tunnel?
explanation: The command 'show ip route' displays the routing table, allowing you to verify if traffic is correctly routed over the VPN tunnel.

stem: A VPN tunnel shows UP but no traffic is passing. What could be a reason related to NAT?
explanation: If NAT exemption is not configured for traffic going through the VPN, it may get translated and not reach the destination.

stem: DNS works internally but not for external domains. What could be a misconfiguration to check first?
explanation: If the firewall is blocking UDP port 53 outbound, DNS queries for external domains will fail, despite internal resolution working.

stem: A website loads slowly from one branch office. Which command would you use to measure the round-trip time to the web server?
explanation: The 'ping' command tests connectivity and measures round-trip time to the web server, helping identify latency issues.

stem: A VPN tunnel shows UP but no traffic is passing. What command would you run to check the interesting traffic ACL?
explanation: The command 'show access-lists' allows you to verify if the interesting traffic ACL is correctly configured to allow traffic through the VPN.

stem: A website loads slowly from one branch office. Which of the following tests would help identify WAN link utilization?
explanation: An iperf test can measure the bandwidth and performance of the WAN link, helping to identify if it is the cause of the slow website loading.

stem: On a Cisco router, show crypto isakmp sa shows QM_IDLE for the peer, and show crypto ipsec sa shows #pkts encaps increasing while #pkts decaps stays at 0. Users at the local site cannot reach the remote LAN. What is the most likely cause?
options: Phase 1 failed because of a pre-shared key mismatch

Return traffic from the remote site is not reaching this router encrypted, for example because the remote crypto ACL does not mirror the local one, the remote NAT translates the traffic before encryption, or ESP is filtered on the path
The crypto map is not applied to the local outside interface
The local transform set does not match the remote peer's transform set
explanation: As the lesson 'Security Interview Scenarios and Troubleshooting' explains (chapter 'Troubleshooting VPN Encryption/Decryption Issues', 36:17), encryption working on one side while decryption counters stay at zero points at the far side or the path: mismatched ACLs, NAT or the peer configuration. QM_IDLE proves Phase 1 is up, an existing IPsec SA proves the transform sets matched, and increasing encaps proves the local crypto map is applied.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: R1 pings 172.16.10.3 sourced from Loopback1. show crypto isakmp sa shows the peer in state QM_IDLE, and show crypto ipsec sa on R1 shows #pkts encaps increasing while #pkts decaps stays at 0. What is the most likely cause?
options: R1 is encrypting and sending, but no encrypted replies come back from R3, for example because R3's replies are not being encrypted or ESP is dropped on the return path.
Phase 1 has failed, so no IPsec SA exists yet.
The pre-shared keys on R1 and R3 do not match.
R1's transform set uses tunnel mode, which blocks return traffic.
explanation: As the lesson 'IPsec VPN Lab: IKEv1 Policy-Based Configuration' shows (chapter 'Verifying VPN Status and Tunnel Details', 56:22), show crypto ipsec sa counts packets encrypted and decrypted. QM_IDLE proves Phase 1 and the pre-shared keys are fine, and rising encaps with zero decaps means the problem is on the return direction from R3.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: The IPsec tunnel between PA1 and PA2 is up, the tunnel addresses 10.30.30.1 and 10.30.30.2 ping each other, and routes for the remote LANs point into the tunnel, but PC 10.11.11.5 cannot ping PC 10.26.26.5. Which two items must be configured on each firewall? (Choose two)
options: A second IKE gateway for the LAN traffic
A security rule from the LAN zone to the Tunnel zone
A source NAT rule translating LAN addresses to the WAN interface address for VPN traffic
A security rule from the Tunnel zone to the LAN zone
A route for the tunnel subnet through the WAN gateway
explanation: As the lesson 'Palo Alto IPsec Site-to-Site VPN' explains (chapter 'Implementing Security Policies for Tunnel Communication', 36:03), each firewall needs rules allowing LAN to Tunnel and Tunnel to LAN, because traffic enters from the tunnel on one side and leaves into it on the other. Source NAT would hide the private addresses the remote side routes back to, and no extra IKE gateway or WAN route is needed.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: On Site A, show crypto isakmp sa shows QM_IDLE and show crypto ipsec sa shows pkts encaps increasing while pkts decaps stays at 0. Which two causes are consistent with this output? (Choose two)
options: A device in the path drops ESP (IP protocol 50) traveling toward Site A
The transform sets do not match, so no IPsec SA exists
Site B lacks a route that sends replies for Site A's LAN out its crypto map interface
UDP port 500 is blocked between the peers
explanation: As the lesson 'ISAKMP Header, SPI and ESP Header Analysis' explains (chapter 'CLI Verification: Crypto IPsec SA and Tunnel Status', 60:00), QM_IDLE and rising encaps prove Phase 1 and the IPsec SA are up, so return traffic is what is missing. That happens if returning ESP is dropped or the peer does not route replies into the tunnel; a Phase 1, UDP 500 or transform set failure would leave no SA to encrypt with.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: R1 and R3 have matching ISAKMP policies, keys and mirrored crypto ACLs, but R1's transform set is esp-3des esp-md5-hmac and R3's is esp-aes esp-sha-hmac. Interesting traffic is sent from R1. What does the engineer observe?
options: Phase 1 fails in MM_NO_STATE because the transform set is part of the ISAKMP policy
Phase 1 completes (QM_IDLE in show crypto isakmp sa), but Quick Mode fails, so there are no IPsec SAs and traffic is not protected
The peers settle on the strongest common algorithms and the tunnel comes up
Phase 2 comes up with R1's transform set because R1 initiated
explanation: As the lesson 'IPsec Aggressive Mode and Site-to-Site VPN Configuration' explains (chapter 'Verification of Phase 1 and Phase 2 Tunnels', 47:33), the ISAKMP policy governs Phase 1 and the transform set governs Phase 2, so show crypto isakmp sa shows the IKE SA while show crypto ipsec sa shows none. The initiator cannot impose its proposal: Quick Mode needs a transform the responder also accepts.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: A crypto map VPN between R1 and R3 has Phase 1 and Phase 2 SAs up. On R1, show crypto ipsec sa shows pkts encaps increasing and pkts decaps at 0; on R3, decaps increase and encaps stays at 0. Which two are likely causes? (Choose two)
options: UDP 500 is blocked between the peers
The pre-shared keys do not match
R3's route to R1's protected subnet points out an interface that has no crypto map
The destination host behind R3 has no route or default gateway back to R3
The transform sets on R1 and R3 do not match
explanation: As the lesson 'Site-to-Site VPN Packet Analysis and Overlapping VPN' explains (chapter 'Troubleshooting and Configuration Errors', 14:53), you check routing and reachability as well as the crypto configuration. Here R3 decrypts R1's traffic but never encrypts replies, so the replies are not reaching R3's crypto interface. Blocked UDP 500, key mismatches or transform set mismatches would have stopped the SAs forming at all.

verification.by: blind check by a second model (Claude Sonnet), workflow wf_5b81b3ed-71b, wf_5aa45911-9b5, wf_427e1487-0b9

stem: In the overlapping-subnet lab, show nat detail on ASA1 shows the twice NAT rule, but show crypto ipsec sa shows no SA after pinging from Site A. Which two misconfigurations would explain this? (Choose two)
options: ASA2's crypto ACL is the mirror image: 172.16.20.0/24 to 172.16.10.0/24
ASA1's crypto ACL matches the real subnet 10.11.11.0/24 instead of the translated 172.16.10.0/24
The NAT rule uses identity NAT for the destination subnet
The pre-shared keys under the two tunnel-groups differ
IKEv1 is enabled on the outside interface of each ASA
explanation: As the lesson 'Overlapping Site-to-Site VPN with Cisco ASA' explains (chapters 'Static NAT Configuration on ASA Firewalls', 22:41, and 'VPN Configuration (IPsec Tunnel Setup)', 32:18), the crypto ACL must match post-NAT addresses, and the peers must share the same pre-shared key. A mirrored ACL on ASA2, destination identity NAT and IKEv1 on outside are all part of the working design.
